title: De Fide Catholica Ex Veteri Et Novo Testamento Contra Judeos
author: Isidorus Hispalensis

passages.original: : Circum dederunt me 36 cenes multi, concilium malignantium obsedit me (Psal, XXI, 17). Canum autem nomen in ens est etiam per prophetam alterum constitutum. In Isaia enirn scriptum est : Omnes canes cæci, nescientes latrare. Canum enim mos est, ut ait noster Hilarius, Pastori alludere, gregem nosse, insidiantes feras persequi. At vero isti cæci canes, pastorem suum non videntes, officium non intelligentes, latratus suos a feris ad gregem, a furibus ad Dominum re- torserunt.
passages.english: "Many dogs have surrounded me; the council of the wicked has besieged me" (Ps. 21:17). And the name of dogs is also assigned to them by another prophet. For in Isaiah it is written: "All [are] blind dogs, not knowing how to bark." For it is the habit of dogs, as our Hilary says, to fawn on the shepherd, to know the flock, and to pursue the wild beasts that lie in wait. But these blind dogs, not seeing their shepherd and not understanding their duty, have turned their barking away from the wild beasts onto the flock, and away from the thieves onto the Lord.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "36 cenes" read as "canes" ("36" taken as a stray mark); "in ens" read as "in eos" ("to them"); "enirn" as "enim"; "re- torserunt" as "retorserunt". "Alludere" is taken in the sense "to fawn on, play up to". Psalm numbering follows the Vulgate.
